paragraphs.title: David Becomes King over All Israel

easy.explanation: All Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron.
easy.q: Where did all Israel gather to David?

easy.explanation: David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD.
easy.q: What did David make with the elders of Israel?

easy.explanation: They anointed David king over Israel.
easy.q: What did the elders do to David?

answers: They were his bone and flesh
medium.explanation: They said, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
medium.q: How did Israel describe their relationship to David?

answers: Led Israel out and brought them in
medium.explanation: The people said David had led out and brought in Israel.
medium.q: What had David done when Saul was king?

medium.explanation: The LORD said David would be ruler over His people Israel.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “ruler” mean in this passage?

answers: The people’s recognition and the LORD’s word
challenge.explanation: Israel recognized David, and his anointing agreed with the word of the LORD.
challenge.q: What two foundations supported David’s kingship?

challenge.explanation: David made the covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD.
challenge.q: Where did David make the covenant with the elders?

challenge.explanation: Israel gathered, David made a covenant with the elders, and they anointed him king.
challenge.q: What is the order of events in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Capture of Jerusalem and the City of David

easy.explanation: Joab the son of Zeruiah went first up and was chief.
easy.q: Who went up first and became chief?

easy.explanation: They called it the city of David.
easy.q: What was the city called after David dwelt in the castle?

answers: He would be chief and captain
medium.explanation: David said that man would be chief and captain.
medium.q: What reward did David promise the first man to smite the Jebusites?

medium.explanation: The KJV says Joab repaired the rest of the city.
medium.q: What did Joab do to the rest of the city?

medium.explanation: The castle was the fortified stronghold where David dwelt.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “castle”?

answers: The Jebusites gave it that name
challenge.explanation: Because David dwelt in the castle, they called it the city of David.
challenge.q: Why was the place called the city of David?

answers: The LORD of hosts was with him
The LORD removed him from the city
challenge.explanation: David waxed greater because the LORD of hosts was with him.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between David’s success and God?

answers: The stronghold was taken, David dwelt there, and the city was repaired
Joab became king, the city was abandoned, and David returned to Hebron
The city was built, Jebus was abandoned, and the castle was left
challenge.explanation: David took the castle, dwelt there, and the city was built and repaired around it.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events?

paragraphs.title: David’s First Mighty Men and the Battle at Pas-dammim

easy.explanation: Jashobeam was the chief of the captains.
He lifted up his spear against three hundred slain by him at one time.
easy.q: How many did Jashobeam slay at one time?

easy.explanation: Eleazar the son of Dodo was with David there.
easy.q: Who was with David at Pas-dammim?

medium.explanation: The Philistines were gathered together there to battle.
medium.q: What were the Philistines doing at Pas-dammim?

answers: The mighty men stood and delivered the field
medium.explanation: The mighty men stood in the parcel and delivered it.
medium.q: What happened when the people fled before the Philistines?

medium.explanation: A parcel of ground is a piece or portion of land.

answers: They stood against the enemy when others fled
challenge.explanation: They set themselves in the midst of the field even after the people fled.
challenge.q: What does the account emphasize about the mighty men?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says, the LORD saved them by a great deliverance.
challenge.q: To whom does the passage attribute the great deliverance?

answers: They stood and fought, and the field was delivered
They fled, and the Philistines won
They made a covenant, and the field was abandoned
challenge.explanation: Their stand and victory resulted in the delivery of the parcel of ground.
challenge.q: What relationship between the warriors’ action and the result is shown?

paragraphs.title: The Three Warriors and the Water of Bethlehem

easy.explanation: Three of the thirty captains went down to David.
easy.q: How many captains went down to David?

answers: Water from the brook of Adullam
easy.explanation: David longed for water from the well of Bethlehem at the gate.
easy.q: What did David long to drink?

answers: He poured it out to the LORD
easy.explanation: David would not drink it, but poured it out to the LORD.
easy.q: What did David do with the water?

answers: They asked the Philistines for it
They broke through the Philistine host and drew it
They found it in the cave of Adullam
medium.explanation: They broke through the host and drew water from the well.
medium.q: How did the three obtain the water?

answers: He regarded it as the blood of men who risked their lives
medium.explanation: David said he could not drink the blood of men who had put their lives in jeopardy.
medium.q: Why would David not drink the water?

answers: He offered it before the LORD
medium.explanation: David poured the water out to the LORD as an offering.
medium.q: What does “poured it out” mean here?

answers: He valued their lives more than the water
challenge.explanation: David treated the water as representing the lives they had risked.
challenge.q: What does David’s refusal to drink show?

challenge.explanation: The Philistines’ garrison was at Bethlehem.

answers: They drew water, entered the camp, and brought it
They broke through the camp, drew water, and brought it to David
They brought it to David, entered the camp, and drew it
challenge.explanation: They first broke through the host, then drew the water, and brought it to David.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the three warriors’ actions?

easy.explanation: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the three.
easy.q: Who was chief of the three?

easy.explanation: Benaiah slew two lionlike men of Moab.

answers: He set him over his guard
He made him ruler of Bethlehem
He made him an elder of Israel
easy.explanation: David set Benaiah over his guard.
easy.q: What position did David give Benaiah?

answers: Fighting Moabites, a lion, and an Egyptian
Building a city, drawing water, and prophesying
Anointing David, making a covenant, and offering sacrifice
medium.explanation: Benaiah fought Moabites, killed a lion, and slew an Egyptian.
medium.q: For which three exploits was Benaiah known?

answers: He took his spear and slew him with it
He made a covenant with him
medium.explanation: He plucked the spear from the Egyptian’s hand and slew him with his own spear.
medium.q: What did Benaiah do to the Egyptian?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes Benaiah as a man of many notable deeds.

answers: He was chief of the three but did not attain to the first three
He was outside the mighty men
challenge.explanation: Abishai was their captain, yet he attained not to the first three.
challenge.q: What was Abishai’s rank in relation to the three?

answers: David recognized his valor and gave him command
challenge.explanation: Benaiah’s deeds and honor led David to place him over the guard.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David setting Benaiah over his guard?

answers: In a pit on a snowy day
At night by the city gate
challenge.explanation: He went down and slew a lion in a pit in a snowy day.
challenge.q: Under what unusual conditions did Benaiah slay the lion?

paragraphs.title: The List of the Military Heroes

answers: A list of David’s valiant men
easy.explanation: The verses list the valiant men of David’s armies.
easy.q: What do these verses mainly present?

easy.explanation: Asahel is identified as the brother of Joab.
easy.q: Who was called the brother of Joab?

easy.explanation: The passage calls him Uriah the Hittite.

answers: Names, descriptions, and places of origin
medium.explanation: The list gives names, titles or descriptions, and places of origin.
medium.q: What kinds of details appear in the list?

answers: The men had varied places and backgrounds
medium.explanation: The list includes men from different places and backgrounds.
medium.q: What can be seen from the names in the list?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes courageous and capable military men.
medium.q: What does “valiant men of the armies” mean?

challenge.explanation: Adina is called the Reubenite and a captain of the Reubenites.
challenge.q: What geographical detail is given about Adina?

answers: The list included men connected with different peoples or regions
challenge.explanation: The names show that David’s forces included men of varied backgrounds.
challenge.q: What does the inclusion of men such as Uriah and Ithai suggest?

answers: A detailed account of every battle
challenge.explanation: The list focuses on names, descriptions, and origins rather than detailed battle narratives.
challenge.q: What kind of information is not the main focus of the list?
